newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was unevenly steady on light to moderate demand and offerings during this shortened holiday trading period, USDA said its weekly meat report.
Retail demand was mostly for immediate needs, while forward interest was rather light.

Improved export demand helped stimulate chuck cuts higher early in the trading period but these cuts were struggling to maintain the newly acquired price levels at weeks end. Round cuts also started the week trading higher but had lost most of the earlier advances by weeks end.
Rib and loin cuts traded mostly lower with top butts and tenderloins experiencing the most downward pressure.

Closely trimmed items followed suit with the commodity product as chuck and round cuts traded higher, while loins cuts traded lower. Trade on beef trimmings was generally steady on mostly moderate demand and offerings.
Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items shipped for immediate needs traded at steady levels, while product delivered in mid July traded lower.

For the week Select and Choice rib primal steady to 2.50 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal 1.00 to 2.00 higher; Select and Choice round primal .50 higher; Select and Choice loin primal 2.00 to 3.00 lower; Closely trimmed item's unevenly steady; Beef trimmings generally steady.
Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items steady to 5.00 lower.
The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn .30 at 100.97; 700/850 Dn .31 at 100.56; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn .15 at 95.85; 700/850 Dn .53 at 94.73.
